notes:
In module ietf-te (Section 5.4), grouping path-forward-properties is used inside /te:te/te:tunnels/te:tunnel/te:primary-paths/te:primary-path, immediately before sibling container primary-reverse-path, which correctly constrains itself to the enclosing tunnel via:

   when "../../../te:bidirectional = 'true'";

However, leaf co-routed in grouping path-forward-properties uses the unbound absolute XPath expression:

   when "/te:te/te:tunnels/te:tunnel/te:bidirectional = 'true'"

Because XPath 1.0 "=" over a node-set is existential (RFC 7950 Section 6.4), this expression evaluates to true for EVERY tunnel in /te:te/te:tunnels/te:tunnel whenever ANY single tunnel on the system has bidirectional = true. Consequently, standards-compliant YANG 1.1 validators (verified with yangson) erroneously accept co-routed = true (and instantiate its default) on unidirectional tunnels (bidirectional = false) whenever any unrelated bidirectional tunnel is configured, contradicting the when description ("Applicable to bidirectional tunnels only.") and diverging from sibling primary-reverse-path (which properly rejects configuration on the same unidirectional tunnel).

Using the relative path "../../../te:bidirectional = 'true'" (co-routed -> primary-path -> primary-paths -> tunnel -> bidirectional) binds the check to the enclosing tunnel instance, passes pyang --ietf --strict with zero errors/warnings, preserves all RFC 10057 Appendix A examples, and rejects co-routed on unidirectional tunnels even when other bidirectional tunnels exist.
